newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Seguin calls for looser euro.
newsitem.headline: France's Seguin calls for looser euro.

text.p: The European Union must not enforce niggling conditions in deciding which countries qualify for a single European currency and should allow as many as possible to join, French National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin said.

Seguin, tipped as a possible prime minister if the centre-right wins the a parliamentary election runoff on Sunday, also said he hoped an economic straightjacket could be eased once the launch of the euro removed the need to reassure the German public about abandoning the deutschemark.

"We are in a straightjacket. I dare hope that once the euro is launched and we no longer need to convince German public opinion, we will loosen it," he said in an interview with weekly magazine L'Express to be published on Wednesday.
"There should not be an apothecary's approach to the entry conditions for the euro. The maximum number of countries must participate," Seguin said.
He also said the fight against inflation must not be the only preoccupation. Employment was "the priority of priorities".

"A target of three percent of deficits in a period of expansion is not virtuous. In a period of austerity it is masochism," Seguin said. But he added that Paris must honour the Maastricht treaty since "France's signature is committed....That signature must be honoured."
